name: Jarha
title: The Egyptian Servant Who Was Incorporated into the Tribe of Judah
summary: Jarha was an Egyptian servant belonging to Sheshan, a descendant of Judah through the Jerahmeel clan. Because Sheshan had no sons, he gave his daughter to Jarha as a wife so that the family line could continue. Through this marriage, Jarha was incorporated into the people of Israel, and his descendants are mentioned in 1 Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Jarha Mentioned as Sheshan's Servant
keyEvents.description: Jarha is introduced as an Egyptian servant in Sheshan's household. He belonged to a foreign nation but became part of the lineage of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Sheshan Gives His Daughter to Jarha
keyEvents.description: Because Sheshan had no sons, only daughters, he gave his daughter to his Egyptian servant Jarha as a wife to ensure the continuation of the family line.

keyEvents.title: Attai Born as Jarha's Son
keyEvents.description: Jarha and Sheshan's daughter had a son named Attai, who continued the family line and became the ancestor of many descendants in Judah.

keyEvents.title: Jarha's Descendants Listed
keyEvents.description: From Attai, the family line continues through many generations, including Nathan, Zabad, Eflal, and several others, as described in the genealogy of Jerahmeel.
